title: Accessing and Slicing Python Strings

understand.concept: String indexing selects one character, while slicing selects a substring using start:stop:step. Indexes start at zero; negative indexes count from the end. The stop position is excluded, omitted boundaries use sequence defaults, and a slice safely clips boundaries that extend beyond the string.
understand.whyItMatters: Indexing and slicing extract identifiers, file extensions, prefixes, suffixes and portions of user-entered text without manually rebuilding every character.
understand.analogy: Think of a string as numbered lockers: indexing opens one locker, while slicing selects a run of lockers with the final boundary left outside the selection.
understand.analogyLimit: Real string indexes are positions in a Unicode sequence, not physical lockers or necessarily visible grapheme clusters. Slices create a new string and never edit the source.

explain.narrative:
## Indexing
Use `text[index]` to select one code point. The first position is 0 and the last is `len(text) - 1`. Negative indexes count backward: -1 selects the final code point. An invalid single index raises `IndexError`.

## Slicing
Use `text[start:stop]`; start is included and stop is excluded. Omitting start means the beginning, and omitting stop means the end. Add a step with `text[start:stop:step]`. A negative step traverses backward. Unlike a single index, slice boundaries outside the sequence are clipped rather than raising `IndexError`.

## Practical checks
Remember the exclusive stop boundary. An empty slice is valid. A step of zero raises `ValueError`. Use `len()` to reason about valid indexes, and test empty strings before indexing.

examples.title: Select a character
examples.explanation: Index 1 is the second character because indexing begins at zero.

examples.title: Select from the end
examples.explanation: Negative indexes count backward from the end; -1 is the final character.

examples.title: Take a bounded slice
examples.explanation: The slice includes positions 1, 2 and 3 but excludes stop position 4.

examples.title: Omit a slice boundary
examples.explanation: An omitted start uses the beginning; an omitted stop uses the end.

examples.title: Use a step and reverse
examples.explanation: A step of 2 selects every second code point; a step of -1 reverses the sequence.
